get.summary: Get the compact width/height/month geometry of a timeline view, in full or paged
get.description: A 6-byte binary record per shot (w:u16, h:u16, month:u16 = year*12+month), with no identifier: it only describes heights, it does not identify assets. Without `limit`: the whole view, with the same filters and the same visibility as /timeline, and 304 support via If-None-Match. With `limit`: only the first N shots (cold screen on a slow network) — if there is more, the response carries the x-keeppix-geometry-cursor header to pass as `cursor` on the next request; no header = that was the whole view. Paged requests do not validate If-None-Match: they are meant for the first load, not for returning to an unchanged view.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Only the first N shots, instead of the whole view

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from the previous page

200.description: 8-byte header (version, count) + N 6-byte records (w, h, month), little-endian

head.summary: Get the true received-bytes offset of an upload session
head.description:
# Errors
`403` if the caller is not the owner of the session. `410` if it has
expired.

200.description: True offset in the Upload-Offset header

403.description: Not the owner of the session

patch.summary: Append a chunk, finalizing the session when complete
patch.description:
# Errors
`403`/`410` as in [`head`]. `409` if `Upload-Offset` does not match the
real `received_bytes` — never a silent acceptance that corrupts the
file. `400` if a required header is missing or the body is empty.
`413` if the chunk exceeds `MAX_CHUNK_BYTES` or the session's remaining
bytes: the body is read in streaming, never buffered whole in RAM.
`460` if the chunk's checksum does not match: the chunk is not written,
the client can resend it without losing the previous offset. `422` at
full-file time, if the end-to-end hash does not match `expected_hash`
or the file is not decodable — never ends up in the library, the
temporary file is deleted, the session is marked failed.

204.description: Chunk accepted, session not yet complete

403.description: Not the owner of the session

409.description: Upload-Offset does not match received_bytes

AlbumBadgeView.description:
An album an asset belongs to, as shown by the ALBUM section of the
lightbox info panel — id and name only: the chips are not clickable and
do not distinguish manual from dynamic.

rule.description:
Present if the album can be refreshed with `POST .../refresh`
(there is no dynamic album, only a filter that re-runs when the
user asks for it).

AppPasswordCreatedView.description:
Creation response: **the only one** where `secret` appears. No other
route ever returns it again — after this response, only the hash
remains.

AppPasswordView.description: Public summary: never `secret`, never the hash.

AssetExifDetailView.description:
Full EXIF of an asset — unlike [`AssetView::camera_model`] (a single
string), the lightbox shows lens, exposure (aperture/shutter/ISO), and
focal length.

AssetFaceBadgeView.description:
A confirmed face, as the UI shows it: only the identity of the person
(bbox/scores are not needed for a filter chip).

person_name.description:
`None` for an unnamed person ("Person 4" — the fallback label is
the frontend's job, as with the other People screens).

favorite.description:
"Favorite": an axis independent from `pick`, not an alias for it.
`false` if absent on write, like the other fields of this body — it
is a full replacement of the vote, not a patch.

AssetTagBadgeView.description:
A confirmed tag, as the UI shows it: name and color for the chip,
`category_id` for the AND between the "Tags"/"Categories" dimensions —
never a need for a second round trip on the tag to resolve its
category.

AssetTagDetailView.description:
A tag as shown by the lightbox info panel — raw `state`/`source`, the
view chooses the rendering (solid / `.ai-applied` / dashed), not this
response.

camera_model.description:
Camera confirmed from the exif ("Camera" dimension). `None` if the
asset has no readable `asset_exif` or the exif does not carry the
model. Additive field.

faces.description:
Confirmed faces ("People" dimension) — `person_id IS NOT NULL AND
rejected_at IS NULL`, assigned by hand or by automatic clustering.
Empty, never absent. Additive field.

favorite.description:
"Favorite" of the **caller**. `AssetView` is shared across many
views, but this field is per-user: two callers on the same `Asset`
can read different values. Defaults to `false` until resolved with
[`Self::with_favorite`] using the caller's set
(`FlagRepo::get`/`favorites_among`). Additive field.

oneOf.description:
Full EXIF ("SHOT" section) — populated **only** by [`asset`] (one
asset's detail, the lightbox), never by [`page`]/`/search`: an extra
query round trip for every row of every timeline page serves no one
there. Additive field, always absent (not `null`) on bulk views.

raw_kind.description:
Badge: `"raw"` / `"jpeg"` / `"raw+jpeg"`. `None` for a kind that is
neither (video, unknown). Additive field.

stack_size.description:
1 if not stacked, otherwise the number of files in the stack.
Additive field.

tags.description:
Confirmed tags ("Tags"/"Categories" dimensions) — only
`state='confirmed'`, never pending proposals. Empty, never absent:
`[]` if the asset has no tags or pgvector is not installed. Additive
field.

AuditEntryView.description:
An audit log entry, with the same schema as `keeppix_db::AuditEntry` —
only the `utoipa` schema lives in the HTTP crate rather than in
`keeppix-db`, which should not need to know about `utoipa`.

originals_warning.description: Mandatory warning when originals are excluded.

culling.description:
Photos still to be culled, summed across all lots of all libraries
with a designated root. `list_lots` is already owner/admin-scoped by
construction — a library without a designated root contributes zero
without an extra query (`list_lots` skips it immediately).

revision.description: Pending tag/face proposals. Zero until there are queues.

asset_ids.description:
HTTP cap: [`crate::batch::MAX_BATCH_ASSETS`]. `apply_batch` is
measured at 5,000 assets under a second.

disk_action.description:
`kept`, `moved_to_trash`, or `purged` — required, same vocabulary as
`DELETE /api/v1/assets/{id}`. No default: the client must always
choose.

hours.description:
Hours to add to `taken_at`. Can be negative — the fix for a camera
clock left wrong after a trip works in both directions.

storage.description:
Free/total space for each visible library — same payload as
`GET /libraries/{id}/storage`, indexed by library id.

BulkOutcome.description:
Outcome of a bulk operation: each element is its own transaction (not
all-or-nothing over the whole batch).

batch_id.description:
Present when the operation recorded an undoable batch.
`flags/batch` leaves it `null`: votes aren't undoable via
`metadata/batch/{id}/undo`.

hashes.description: blake3 hex digests (64 characters) computed locally by the client.

unknown_hashes.description:
The subset of `hashes` that the server **does not** already have:
these are the only ones worth uploading ("I already have these 47,
send me the other 12").

rule.description:
The filter the album is created with. `None` for a purely manual
album, which can then never be refreshed via `refresh`.

hide_metadata.description:
When true, the public asset list omits capture dates and coordinates.
The field name is kept because `/api/v1` is frozen.

name.description:
Empty or absent: unnamed person ("Person 4"). Non-empty: validated
name, cannot be whitespace only.

client_mtime.description:
Original `mtime` on the client device: preserved as a fallback for
`taken_at` when EXIF doesn't have it.

expected_hash.description: blake3 hex digest of the whole file, if the client already knows it.

disk_action.description:
`kept`, `moved_to_trash`, or `purged` — no default: the client must
always choose.

files_untouched.description: Always `true`: deletion only touches the database.

FaceBulkOutcome.description:
Twin of [`BulkOutcome`] typed on [`FaceId`] — the face review queue
works on faces, not assets. Same shape and same [`FailureReason`] as
`BulkOutcome`: `FailureReason::FileMissing` doesn't make sense here (no
filesystem path is involved), but keeping it in the shared enum costs
less than a second taxonomy — the caller simply never produces it for a
face.

FailureReason.description:
Closed taxonomy. The fifth value `Unknown` is honest: better one extra
case than pretending it's one of the other four.

GrantSummaryView.description:
Response body of `POST /permissions` and `PATCH /permissions/{id}`: the
same three keys that used to come out of an ad hoc
`serde_json::json!(...)`, now with a type `utoipa` can describe.

tolerance_minutes.description:
Defaults to five minutes if absent. Outside the covered range, the
endpoint is used only within this tolerance.

culling_root_folder_id.description:
Root for folder-based culling. `None` until the owner designates
one — culling behaves as before, no new behavior is forced.

faces_enabled.description: Face recognition toggle for this library.

item_count.description:
Items shared by this link (e.g. `"246 items"`). Brought back because
the "My shares" card explicitly requests it for public links.

view_count.description: Accesses of the link, not "shared items" — that's `item_count`.

totp_code.description: Optional TOTP or recovery code. Required once the account has 2FA enabled.

folder_id.description:
Id of `cover_asset_id`'s folder: opens "Open folder" from the
popover without a second request.

place_label.description:
Human-readable place label, from reverse geocoding.
`None` until the cover asset has an assigned place.

cover_asset_id.description: Explicit `null` removes the cover; absent = unchanged.

folder_id.description: Id of the folder chosen as root, or `null` to remove it.

name.description:
Absent: name unchanged. Empty string: clears the name. Non-empty
string: new name (rejected if whitespace only).

parent_id.description: Absent = unchanged; `null` = detach from the parent.

PermissionGrantView.description:
Entry of `GET /permissions` — replaces the `keeppix_db::PermissionGrantView`
served directly before: same JSON keys (`id`/`subject_id` stay strings,
nothing changes on the wire), but with a `utoipa` schema instead of
having to add one to `keeppix-db`, which knows nothing about HTTP.

face_count.description:
Present for `GET /persons` (list); absent for single-person
responses, which don't pay for a second query round trip to count.

Problem.description:
RFC 9457-formatted error. The `type` field is a stable code clients can
branch on; `title` is in English and is meant for debugging, not the
end user — translation happens in the frontend.

It's also a schema in the `OpenAPI` document: it's the shape the mobile
client branches on, so it needs to be described, not just served.

ProblemView.description:
A row of the composed flat list: unlike the raw buckets below, it
arrives already in natural language in the request's language, with
the proposed action ready for a UI button.

problems.description:
Composed flat list. Additive: the three raw buckets above stay to
avoid breaking a client that was already reading them.

ProposalView.description:
An AI-matched proposal pending human review. Enriched with the tag name
and filename: the review queue must not make a second round trip per
row.

PublicAssetView.description:
Subset of [`AssetView`] safe for an anonymous guest — deliberately
**not** `AssetView` itself: that type is shared with timeline/search and
is meant to grow "additive" fields (`tags`, `faces`, `full_exif`, …, see
the comments on `AssetView`), and reusing it here would expose every
future addition to an anonymous user without anyone noticing. A privacy
test enforces this structurally: it walks the whole body and rejects
any "face"/"person" key, so even `faces:[]` (empty, never populated by
this route) fails it — on purpose, because if someone later copies
`.with_faces(...)` from `timeline.rs` into this route, it would fail
the same way, not only the case with real data.

preview_token.description: Required on apply; returned by preview. Absent on preview requests.

RenameAccepted.description:
Response of `apply_batch`/`undo_batch` (`202`): the outcome is not yet
known when responding — the caller follows `operation_id` over the
`WebSocket` (`operation.progress`), the same pattern as `ScanAccepted`
(`routes/libraries.rs`).

keep.description:
Id of the asset to keep: all other non-trashed members of the group
receive `disk_action`.

resolved.description: How many members were touched (the group minus `keep`).

dry_run.description: When true, only simulate — no writes.

operation_id.description:
Present only when **this** request is the one that actually
follows the queued job: if a scan for the same library was already
`pending`/`running` — queued by the watcher or an earlier request —
that one wins via the shared `dedup_key`, and this response has no
operation of its own to offer.

eta_seconds.description: Always `null` for now: no estimate until there is measured throughput.

SharedWithMeView.description:
Entry of `GET /shared-with-me` ("Shared with me"). Same observation as
[`PermissionGrantView`]: only the schema moves, nothing else changes.

SuggestionKindView.description:
A closed set: `tag` is already in the shape even before it gains a
source, so the contract doesn't change twice.

assignment_count.description:
How many rows in `asset_tags` would be deleted along with the tag.
The UI confirmation dialog reads this before the DELETE.

batch_id.description:
Kept for additive `/api/v1` compatibility; same value as
[`BulkOutcome::batch_id`].

preview_token.description: Opaque token to pass to the apply endpoint within 5 minutes.

qr_svg.description: Inline SVG QR of `otpauth_uri` — the SPA renders it without a QR dependency.

collision.description:
`created`, `skipped_duplicate`, or `renamed`: never a silent
overwrite, always reported to the client.

UserView.description:
Public representation of a user. Contains neither the password hash nor
the TOTP secret: those fields never leave the database.

password_changed_at.description:
When the password was last set ("Last changed"). Matches account
creation until it is changed.

session_cookie.description: Session cookie issued by POST /api/v1/setup and POST /api/v1/auth/login.
